provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Review of JSS 2 Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the basic hair styling techniques learned in JSS 2.
The students should be able to demonstrate simple makeup application procedures.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about basic hair care and simple makeup looks. Today we will revise these important foundation skills before moving to more advanced techniques.

Content:
Hair styling recap includes washing, conditioning, and simple braiding. We also covered basic makeup like foundation application and lip color. Remember to always use clean tools and test products on skin first. For example, when fixing hair at a local market stall, you should keep your combs and brushes clean to prevent scalp infections.

Class activity:
Students will pair up and practice basic braiding techniques on each other while discussing the importance of clean tools.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three basic hair care steps?
2. Why is it important to test makeup products before use?
3. How does proper tool care affect customer satisfaction?

Summary:
Today's revision helps us build confidence in our foundational skills before advancing to more complex beauty techniques.

topics.title: Advanced Hair Styling
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list different advanced braiding styles.
The students should be able to demonstrate fixing techniques for various hair types.
The students should be able to explain the process of applying hair extensions.

Introduction:
After reviewing our basic skills from last term, we are now ready to move forward to more complex hair styling techniques that are in high demand in Nigerian salons.

Content:
Advanced braiding styles include cornrows, Ghana weaving, and all-back styling. Fixing involves securing hair properly using pins and bands. Extensions add length and volume through weaves, braids, or bonding. For example, when fixing hair for a wedding, you might use Ghana weaving with extensions to create an elegant updo that lasts throughout the Harmattan season.

Class activity:
Students will practice creating three different advanced braiding styles on mannequins using extension hair.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two advanced braiding styles.
2. What is the purpose of using hair extensions?
3. How would you fix very fine hair without causing damage?

Summary:
Mastering these advanced techniques will make you more valuable as a beauty professional in the Nigerian beauty industry.

topics.title: Hair Coloring and Relaxing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the safety measures for hair coloring and relaxing.
The students should be able to explain the steps in hair coloring process.
The students should be able to differentiate between various hair relaxer types.

Introduction:
Building on our styling knowledge, we now explore how to chemically alter hair through coloring and relaxing, which requires careful attention to safety and proper techniques.

Content:
Hair coloring involves applying color to achieve desired shades. Relaxing straightens curly or kinky hair. Safety measures include patch testing, using gloves, and working in well-ventilated areas. For example, when relaxing hair at a salon in Lagos, you must first test the relaxer on a small strand to ensure the client won't have an adverse reaction, similar to how market women test pepper before selling.

Class activity:
Students will practice mixing hair color and applying it to swatches while wearing proper protective equipment.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is patch testing important before hair relaxing?
2. List three safety measures for hair coloring.
3. What would you do if a client complains of scalp burning during relaxing?

Summary:
Proper knowledge of coloring and relaxing techniques combined with strict safety measures ensures excellent results and protects both client and stylist.

topics.title: Hair Treatment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the importance of deep conditioning.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper scalp care techniques.
The students should be able to identify suitable treatments for different hair problems.

Introduction:
After learning about styling and chemical treatments, we now focus on how to maintain healthy hair through proper treatments and care, especially important in our Nigerian climate.

Content:
Deep conditioning restores moisture and nutrients to hair. Scalp care involves cleansing, massaging, and moisturizing the scalp. Different treatments address specific issues like dandruff, dryness, or breakage. For example, during the dry Harmattan season, deep conditioning treatments are essential to prevent hair damage from the harsh weather, just as we protect our skin with shea butter.

Class activity:
Students will create a hair treatment plan for different hair types and conditions found in Nigeria.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is deep conditioning important?
2. How often should scalp care be performed?
3. What treatment would you recommend for someone with an itchy scalp?

Summary:
Regular hair treatments maintain the health and beauty of hair, ensuring that chemical services and styling work last longer and look better.

topics.title: Midterm Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge of all topics covered so far.
The students should be able to apply practical skills learned in previous weeks.

Introduction:
Today's midterm examination will test your understanding of the hair styling, coloring, relaxing, and treatment techniques we have covered in the past four weeks.

Content:
The examination will cover both theoretical questions and practical demonstrations. You will need to identify proper techniques, safety measures, and product uses. For example, you might be asked to demonstrate how to properly apply relaxer while explaining safety precautions, similar to how a market woman explains how to select fresh tomatoes.

Class activity:
Students will complete a written examination and perform practical demonstrations of selected techniques.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the steps for applying hair extensions.
2. What safety measures should be taken during hair relaxing?
3. How does deep conditioning benefit the hair?
4. Demonstrate a basic braiding technique.

Summary:
This midterm assessment helps identify areas where you excel and areas needing improvement before we move to the second half of the term.

topics.title: Skin Care Routine
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the steps in a basic skin care routine.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper facial massage techniques.
The students should be able to explain the importance of exfoliation.

Introduction:
After focusing on hair care, we now shift our attention to skin care, which is equally important in beauty services and requires understanding of different skin types and proper techniques.

Content:
Skin care routine includes cleansing, exfoliation, toning, moisturizing, and sun protection. Exfoliation removes dead skin cells to reveal fresh skin. Facial massage improves circulation and product absorption. For example, when treating a client who works in the dusty Lagos traffic, proper cleansing is essential to remove pollutants before applying other products, just as we wash beans thoroughly before cooking.

Class activity:
Students will practice facial massage techniques on each other using proper skin care products.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the five basic steps of skin care routine?
2. Why is exfoliation important?
3. How would you adapt a skin care routine for oily skin?

Summary:
A proper skin care routine maintains healthy skin and provides a good canvas for makeup application, enhancing overall beauty results.

topics.title: Midterm Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and prepare for the second half of the term.

Introduction:
This is a break period to rest and recharge before continuing with our beauty and cosmetology studies.

Content:
Use this time to review what you have learned so far and practice techniques. Rest is important for both physical and mental health, which affects your ability to learn and perform beauty services effectively. For example, just as a danfo driver needs rest to drive safely, you need rest to learn properly.

Class activity:
No formal class activity during break period.

Evaluation questions:
No evaluation questions during break period.

Summary:
Enjoy your break and return refreshed and ready to continue learning about beauty and cosmetology.

topics.title: Makeup Application Techniques S
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate day makeup application steps.
The students should be able to explain the differences between day and evening makeup.
The students should be able to select appropriate products for different skin tones.

Introduction:
Now that we've covered skin care basics, we will focus on makeup application techniques that enhance natural beauty and address different occasions and skin types.

Content:
Day makeup emphasizes natural looks with light foundation, neutral colors, and minimal products. Evening makeup allows for bolder colors, stronger contours, and more dramatic effects. Product selection should match skin tone and type. For example, when doing makeup for a traditional wedding in the North, you might use brighter colors and heavier application than for office makeup in Lagos.

Class activity:
Students will practice applying both day and evening makeup looks on each other, focusing on proper blending and color selection.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the main difference between day and evening makeup?
2. How do you select foundation for different skin tones?
3. Why is blending important in makeup application?

Summary:
Mastering makeup application techniques allows you to create looks that enhance natural beauty while addressing different client needs and occasions.

topics.title: Nail Extension and Maintenance
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate the steps for applying nail extensions.
The students should be able to explain proper maintenance of artificial nails.
The students should be able to identify safety measures for nail services.

Introduction:
Moving beyond hair and makeup, we now explore nail services, which are in high demand and require precision and proper technique for both application and maintenance.

Content:
Nail extensions add length and strength using acrylic, gel, or fiberglass. Application involves preparing the natural nail, applying product, and shaping. Maintenance includes fills, repairs, and proper removal. Safety measures include sterilization tools and proper product handling. For example, when fixing nails for a client who works with their hands like a market trader, you might recommend stronger gel extensions that can withstand daily activities.

Class activity:
Students will practice applying nail extensions on practice hands using proper techniques and safety measures.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the three main types of nail extensions?
2. How should artificial nails be properly removed?
3. Why is sterilization important in nail services?

Summary:
Proper nail extension application and maintenance ensures client satisfaction and prevents nail damage, making this service valuable in any beauty salon.

topics.title: Salon Hygiene
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list proper disinfection procedures for salon tools.
The students should be able to explain the importance of salon hygiene.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper hand washing techniques.

Introduction:
As we near the end of the term, we focus on salon hygiene, which is crucial for client safety and professional standards in the beauty industry.

Content:
Salon hygiene involves proper cleaning, disinfection, and sterilization of tools and equipment. This prevents the spread of infections and ensures client safety. Hand washing is essential before and after each client. For example, just as a food vendor at a market stall must keep their cooking area clean to prevent illness, a beauty therapist must keep their tools sterile to prevent infections.

Class activity:
Students will practice proper disinfection procedures for various salon tools and demonstrate correct hand washing techniques.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is salon hygiene important?
2. What are the steps for properly disinfecting salon tools?
3. How often should towels and linens be changed in a salon?

Summary:
Maintaining proper salon hygiene protects both clients and practitioners, ensuring a safe and professional environment for beauty services.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate all practical skills learned during the term.
The students should be able to answer questions on all theoretical topics covered.

Introduction:
As we approach the end of the term, we will revise all topics covered to ensure everyone is prepared for the final examination and can demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of beauty and cosmetology.

Content:
We will review hair styling, coloring, relaxing, treatments, skin care, makeup application, nail extensions, and salon hygiene. Focus on both theoretical understanding and practical application. For example, when reviewing hair relaxing techniques, we will discuss both the chemical process and proper safety measures, similar to how we review all steps before cooking a complex dish.

Class activity:
Students will rotate through stations reviewing different practical skills while answering theoretical questions about each area.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the complete hair coloring process.
2. Demonstrate proper facial massage technique.
3. What safety measures should be taken during nail extension application?
4. How does salon hygiene affect client satisfaction?

Summary:
This comprehensive review helps solidify your knowledge and skills, preparing you for success in the final examination and future beauty career.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate all practical skills learned during the term.
The students should be able to answer questions on all theoretical topics covered.

Introduction:
Continuing our revision process, we will focus on areas where students may need additional practice and clarification before the final examination.

Content:
We will concentrate on challenging topics like advanced hair styling techniques, chemical treatments, and makeup application for different occasions. Emphasis will be on proper technique and safety. For example, when practicing makeup for different skin tones, we will discuss how to adjust products and application methods for Igbo, Yoruba, and Hausa clients who may have different undertones.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to create presentations on specific topics, demonstrating both knowledge and teaching ability.

Evaluation questions:
1. How would you adapt a skin care routine for dry skin during Harmattan?
2. Explain the complete process for applying hair extensions.
3. What are the differences between various types of nail extensions?

Summary:
This final revision ensures all students are confident in their abilities and ready to demonstrate their knowledge and skills in the final examination.

topics.title: Examination / Closing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of all topics covered.
The students should be able to apply practical skills effectively.

Introduction:
Today's final examination will assess your overall understanding of beauty and cosmetology principles and your ability to apply the practical skills learned throughout the term.

Content:
The examination includes both written questions and practical demonstrations covering all topics from hair care to nail services. You will need to show proper technique, safety awareness, and product knowledge. For example, you might be asked to demonstrate a complete makeup look while explaining product choices for different occasions, similar to how a chief explains ingredients in a traditional dish.

Class activity:
Students will complete a comprehensive examination testing both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the complete process for hair relaxing with safety measures.
2. Demonstrate day makeup application for an office setting.
3. How would you maintain artificial nails for a client who works with their hands?
4. Why is salon hygiene critical in the beauty industry?

Summary:
This final examination marks the completion of your JSS 3 beauty and cosmetology studies, preparing you for advanced learning in senior secondary school.
